newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Trust 1996/97 problem loan disposal Y20 bln.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Trust 1996/97 problem loan disposal Y20 bln.

text.p: Nippon Trust Bank Ltd said on Friday that it disposed of about 20 billion yen worth of problem loans in the last business year which ended on March 31.
It said in a statement that its estimated operating profit on its core banking business was 16.5 billion yen for 1996/97, against a previously projected 14 billion yen.
The bank is scheduled to announce its 1996/97 business results in late May.
Nippon Trust, the smallest of the nation's seven major trust banks, is a subsidary of Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd.
It said it received financial support of 44.2 billion yen from Tokyo-Mitsubishi in 1996/97, enabling it to post an estimated parent net profit of 40 billion yen in 1996/97.
The bank has been aiming to clear up cumulative losses in 1996/97, it said.
Nippon Trust said it would post a parent current loss of 2.5 billion yen in 1996/97, as it was forced to write down appraisal losses on shareholdings due to stock price declines in 1996/97.

A Nippon Trust official said that the latest earnings forecast did not include expected losses stemming from the failures of three non-bank financial institutions affiliated with Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB).
Banking sources said that Nippon Trust had 4.8 billion yen in loans outstanding to the three affiliates.
The three affiliates on Tuesday filed for bankruptcy in line with NCB's radical restructuring programme, which was also announced that day.
